key_insight: Transient ion current (TIC/BACE) in perovskite solar cells is often limited by transport-layer capacitance, not the perovskite’s true ionic properties.
engineering_relevance: Accurate ion-density and mobility extraction requires accounting for transport-layer thickness, doping, and interface charge storage to avoid large overestimates.
method: Varied C60 electron-transport-layer thickness in p-i-n devices and Spiro-OMeTAD hole-transport-layer doping in n-i-p devices.
Used drift-diffusion simulations to identify the capacitive bottleneck and the saturation limit for measurable ion charge.
Tested correction/extrapolation approaches based on average ionic displacement and transport-layer-thickness trends.
evidence_signal: Experiments across two device architectures confirmed that TIC depends strongly on transport-layer properties and that extrapolating toward a transport-layer-free limit recovers more realistic ionic parameters.
watch_item: TIC can be inflated by transport-layer capacitance, ion penetration, or slow release of trapped carriers, so interpretation must be corrected with care.
paper_title: Overcoming Transport Layer Bottlenecks to Quantify Ionic Parameters from Transient Ion Current Measurements of Perovskite Solar Cells
